objective: Real Cognito authentication for the SPA: an AuthService interface with one implementation over amazon-cognito-identity-js, the sign-up / confirm / sign-in / forgot-password / profile-creation pages, a route guard, and the wiring that feeds the ID token to FRONTEND-001's apiClient token provider.
acceptance_criteria: AuthService is an interface, and every page and hook depends on the interface rather than on the amazon-cognito-identity-js implementation; tests inject a double of the interface and never mock the library.

The implementation exposes signUp, confirmSignUp, resendConfirmationCode, signIn, signOut, forgotPassword, confirmForgotPassword, refreshSession and getIdToken, and no production code branches on environment to choose an implementation.

apiClient's token provider returns the current Cognito ID token, so an authenticated request carries 'Authorization: Bearer <id token>'; it returns null when no session exists, and the request then carries no Authorization header.
A signed-in user whose GET /users/me returns 404 is routed to profile creation, not to an error view.
A signed-in user whose GET /users/me returns 200 is routed to the feed, and profile creation is not reachable for them.
An anonymous user hitting a protected route is redirected to sign-in, and is sent on to the route they originally requested after a successful sign-in.

Profile creation submits POST /users with username and date_of_birth, offers the teams from GET /events/teams as the preferred-team choice, and surfaces a 422 from the age gate as a field-level message rather than a generic failure.
Sign-up, confirm, sign-in and forgot-password each render a field-level error from the corresponding Cognito failure, and none of them logs or renders the pool id, client id or any token.
Every form input has an associated label, every control is reachable by keyboard, and the tests query by role and label rather than by test id.
